answer: A defense is to make each identity expensive to create and slow to trust. A new agent must lock a refundable bond before it can bid, and that bond is slashed if peers prove it submitted fake work or double-spent a credential. Like a sonnet, the rules are strict, so gaming them is visible. Reputation then grows only from completed, checked jobs, not self-reported volume, so a vine of fake accounts cannot quickly outvote honest workers. A bridge between services must check that bond and history on both sides, so an attacker must pay and build history separately for every fake identity.
